session_note: Missouri's 2026 regular session (103rd General Assembly, 2nd Regular Session) convened 2026-01-07 and constitutionally adjourned at 6:00pm on 2026-05-15, the first Friday following the second Monday in May, per Missouri Constitution Article III Section 20(a); confirmed on senate.mo.gov's 'Major Dates for 2026' page, which lists '15 - Last Day of Session (Article III, Section 20(a), Const.)'. All bills remaining on a calendar after that deadline are tabled. Missouri does not carry bills over between annual sessions -- each session is a fresh start, so any bill not truly agreed to and finally passed (and signed) by 2026-05-15 is dead and would need to be refiled with a new bill number in 2027.

new_bills.status: Second Read and Referred to Senate Transportation, Infrastructure and Public Safety Committee 2026-05-07 (last recorded action, 8 days before adjournment); no hearing was scheduled; died without further action at sine die, 2026-05-15
new_bills.key_provisions: Creates provisions relating to the regulation of large load electric customers. Lowers the Public Service Commission tariff-filing threshold for large electrical corporations (over 250,000 customers) from 100 MW to 50 MW of projected annual peak demand (Section 393.130.7). New Section 393.325 requires an owner/operator of a 'large load facility' (a category that includes data centers) intending to operate after 2026-08-28 to file a disclosure of intent with the PSC before signing utility contracts, undergo PSC-reviewed pre- and post-construction studies, bear its own infrastructure costs without shifting them to other ratepayers in general rate cases, contribute to low-income ratepayer assistance programs once operational, and implement an emergency curtailment system (with exemptions for hospitals, long-term care, and first-responder facilities).
